title: Unary minus on BLANK leaves it BLANK

source.quote: the minus operator creates a negative value, if applied to a numeric value
source.supports: unary minus negates a numeric value; it says nothing of BLANK

source.quote: Data models support the unary operator, - (negative), but this operator doesn't change the data type of the operand
source.supports: the operand keeps its type; BLANK has none to change

derivation: No source states the result of unary minus on BLANK. The operator is said not to change the type of its operand, and BLANK is not a numeric value to negate, so BLANK is taken to stay BLANK.
alternative: BLANK is converted to 0 as it is in an addition or subtraction (BLANK - 4 is -4), and the result is 0 (an int64).
notes: The column's type is not asserted: no source says what type this result has.
